_comment: H2 (docs/design/BUSBAR-1.6.0.md THE DESIGN, §1): 'conformance rigs carry one cell per Teller step per plane'.
Steps are the kernel's own StepName::ALL (crates/busbar-contract/src/caps/step.rs; spec #72, BUSBAR-1.6.0.md:2266): arrival, decode,
authenticate, verify, approve, admit, route, meter, audit, encode (THE DESIGN §1, :154, spells the last one exit). This is the plane x step MATRIX: for every cell, either an id that names a
real, run scenario in one of the conformance rigs (or the shadow oracle, for the llm plane), or
the literal string "none" naming a genuine gap. 'gating' marks the 7 steps whose contract H2
spells out explicitly (a refusal/outcome that must never leak past its step); the other 3
(arrival, decode, approve) are mapped for completeness but do not fail the --check by themselves
when a shared, plane-agnostic kernel cell already covers them for every plane at once.
Checked by: cargo xtask gate teller-steps. Wired into scripts/verify-1.6.0-done.sh
beside the ISOMORPHISM group.
THE ROSTER IS DERIVED, NOT WRITTEN: 'steps' must be the kernel's own StepName::ALL
(crates/busbar-contract/src/caps/step.rs, which the kernel's teller imports), as a set AND in loop
order, and the matrix rows must be every PlaneMeta KEY a plane-kind crate (busbar-plane-*) states,
plus any row another crate's own PlaneMeta declares (admin: busbar-core-admin). A plane with no row,
a kernel step the matrix lacks, and a step or row the tree does not declare are each RED.
OWED GAPS: a gating cell that is "none" is RED unless 'owed_gaps' names it ("<plane>.<step>": "<owner>").
The list must be EXACTLY the measured gaps: a gap nobody owes is RED, and an owed entry whose cell
is no longer a gap is RED until it is struck. The list only shrinks; the gate prints it on every run.
THE ROOT COLUMN (`root_legs` + every cell's `root`). The `cell` above is the SHIPPED path: the
step proven where a conformance rig drives the plane as an operator would. Every plane now
also runs through the composition root -- root-llm (the llm door's served leg, behind plane-llm) / root-streaming / root-admin behind their

features, root-mcp / root-a2a on the kernel-loop rider every linked one-shot plane is served through, root-decisions on the decision plane's door served by the root's serve path -- and a step proven on the rig and unwitnessed over the loop is the same half-answer.
So every cell carries a SECOND verdict over its plane's root leg:
proven -- with `test`: a `<the leg's own file under crates/busbar/src/root/>::<test fn>` cell that drives the
step through the loop. The check verifies the file is the leg's own and the fn is in
it; `--root-legs` EXECUTES every one of them with every leg's feature on.
none   -- with `note`: what the leg does instead, and why no cell drives this step yet. R-16:
name a gap, never paper it.
The root column's gaps are PRINTED and named on every run but do not fail --check by themselves.
Every leg's feature (a leg's `feature`, else the leg's own name) is now IN the binary's default feature set, so for
each of them the loop IS the shipped path and --root-legs-gating (below) holds them to the same red
rule the rig column has: a gating step with no cell over the loop fails. A leg whose feature is
default-off is still being switched over plane by plane, so its root gaps remain the switch-over
queue and are printed rather than failed. What IS red on this column whatever the leg ships as: a
`proven` root cell whose named test does not exist, and a leg with no proven cell at all.
The two columns are independent verdicts about the same step and either may be "none" alone:
mcp.approve is exactly that shape today -- open on the rig, proven over the loop.
